# bugs #3763: sdas8051.exe of the 4.4.0 Win64 release crashes on a source line with a syntax error

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3763/
- Category: [Duplicates](../../duplicate.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close as a duplicate of bug #3744. Examine the longjmp call of the q error path in the Win64 release build.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The crash does not occur with sdas8051 built from r17176 on Linux. For the two lines of the
attached `main.s`, the assembler prints `<q> Expected a ','.` for line 1 and a `<u>` error for
line 2 and returns exit status 2. valgrind reports no error for this run. No Windows binary was
run.

## Reason

Bug #3744 shows the same fault for the same binary. The screenshots in both tickets show
`sdas8051.exe` of 4.4.0 #14620 on Windows 6.1.7601 with a fault in `ntdll.dll` and the exception
code `c0000028`.

The assembler raises a `q` error for the input of each ticket. `.include 12345678` from bug #3744
gives a `<q>` error on r17176, because `getdstr` takes the first `1` as the delimiter of the file
name and finds no second `1`. The first line of this ticket gives a `<q>` error from `comma`.
`xerr` in `sdas/asxxsrc/assubr.c` ends every `q` error with `longjmp` to the `setjmp` call in
`main`. r14620 has this code as well.

Microsoft documents `c0000028` as `STATUS_BAD_STACK`, which the stack unwinder raises, and on
64-bit Windows `longjmp` unwinds the stack. The exception code is therefore consistent with a
failure in this `longjmp` call. That was not tested on Windows. Bug #3744 adds two facts. A Win64
binary that a commenter built from the source does not crash, and the reporter found that the
binary of the 32-bit 4.4.0 installer does not crash.
